name: Airtable OAuth Client Per Workspace
description: Airtable OAuth Client Per Workspace describes a customer-managed OAuth setup pattern for granting an integration access to selected Airtable workspaces and bases.
agentUseSummary: This setup pattern is visible as a canonical-provider alias preview. Relay uses the single typed Airtable connector and Airtable's workspace or base resource grants; it will not create duplicate connection state or collect a customer OAuth client secret for each workspace.

capabilities.label: Use workspace-scoped Airtable grants
capabilities.description: Connect the canonical Airtable provider and choose one or more workspaces or bases during Airtable's authorization flow instead of creating a separate client per workspace.

blocked.label: Create duplicate Airtable connection state
blocked.description: A per-workspace client listing must not create a second token lifecycle or runtime tool surface beside the canonical Airtable connector.

blocked.label: Capture a customer OAuth client secret
blocked.description: Relay will not ask a workspace user to paste an Airtable OAuth client secret into this Marketplace alias.

blocked.label: Register an Airtable OAuth integration
blocked.description: OAuth integration creation, legal configuration, redirect registration and secret rotation remain provider-console administration outside Relay agent actions.

blocked.label: Run Airtable tools through this alias
blocked.description: All Airtable runtime actions belong to the canonical airtable connection so ownership, grants, refresh rotation, policy and audits remain unified.

approvalProfiles.label: Canonical Airtable connection required
approvalProfiles.description: This setup alias is not connectable. Airtable authorization, resource grants, tools and policy remain owned by the canonical airtable provider.

runtimeSupport.description: This alias installs no OpenClaw tools; use the canonical Airtable provider for its typed runtime pack.
This alias installs no Hermes tools; use the canonical Airtable provider for its typed runtime pack.

providerSetup.blocker: A per-workspace OAuth client would duplicate Relay's canonical Airtable token lifecycle and require customer-owned client-secret handling, while Airtable already supports selecting workspace or base resources and multiple authorization grants for one integration.
providerSetup.nextAction: Route customers to the canonical airtable provider and preserve workspace/base grant metadata on that connection. If enterprise service-account authorization is needed, extend and test the canonical Airtable connector rather than creating a second provider slug or secret store.

evidence.supports: Airtable documents one OAuth integration client with exact redirects, S256 PKCE, scoped authorization, rotating refresh tokens and developer-held client credentials.
Airtable documents user-selected base or workspace resource grants, multiple distinct authorizations for one integration, manual and admin revocation, and a twenty-grant per-user limit.
Airtable documents enterprise service accounts authorizing an OAuth integration independently of a person, managed from the Admin Panel.
Airtable documents enterprise controls and allowlists for third-party OAuth API access to organization-owned bases and workspaces.
